finding: 0x1200 is right: upstream classic BIF has CAT_BASE0..7 at 0x1200 + 8n, 64-bit, ADDR in bits 39:12 (MASKFULL 0x000000FFFFFFF000); Orchard's A8 uses BIF_CAT_BASE0 0x1200 too. Apple's value is the raw catalogue address (fw +0x1f0 writer with shift 0), which matches upstream's encoding

most likely a filtered host view: META boots and runs from mapped pages through CAT_BASE0, so the catalogue is in effect. Other registers the ConfigRAM or the firmware writes also read 0 or ignore host writes (0x3808 reads 0 after the list writes 1; 0xbc8, 0xb08). The firmware never reads 0x1200 either (no access in the decode)

none found: BIF_MMU_ENTRY/ENTRY_STATUS (0x1290/0x1288) are the MMU's pending-entry status, not a host-driven walker. The fault bank's CAT_BASE field (0) and the absence of further faults are the best evidence that context 0 works
nothing in the kext sets another context for META; the firmware sets other catalogues only for user slots, through MMU_ROOT/TAG_HOST and DeviceSetGARTPhysical (request 19)
